title: Is investing in art worth in this AI age?
author: Free-Version-2746
selftext:
Say need 2 months to dev a game. Now it will need another 5 months to make all assets your own.

Do you thing it is worth? Or take that 5 months to polish gameplays better choice.

comments.author: CharacterTension2896
comments.body: You know I tried making assets many ways. Now I tell it to use Blender and put it on a quality loop with a Qa and visual check to critique and it’s been ok. On the next occasion I wanna start with it making a fully featured game engine for the game. Also, I’ve seen GitHub have some free ways to get assets in. I’ll loop that into the game engine also.

replies.author: darkoblivion000
replies.body:
I have found this is the best way. These LLMs are not visual models, they understand math and angles and geometry but they don’t really have vision. So pixel art and keeping characters consistent through animations and making it look natural I think is hard for them. But rendering a 3d model especially simpler low poly ones seems to come more naturally. I have had it generate more machine related assets and it seems to do quite a good job with it

A lot of issues and the “AI” look I’ve noticed are when people try to make it do smooth pixel art or sprite type animations

comments.author: RageshAntony
comments.body:
If everybody can make burger, why we need to start a restaurant ? 

Art comes from sentient mind filled with consciousness and  conscience. Until AI gets this, it can't produce a quality art.

comments.author: Sencha-Games
comments.body: AI art looks like shit at the moment so I think it's worth investing in either learning art or hiring artists if you want to make something good.

comments.author: Significant-Neck-520
comments.body:
AI is much better for producing the code than it is for producing the assets. The code seems to be very good, while the art, even if impressive, is not up to par with professional work. 

 Maybe it could change in the future, but currently I still think producing the art is worth it, if you have the skills

replies.author: Limp_Bus3865
replies.body: It is not, and you explained why. Because it will soon be on human level

comments.author: PersonalityOk5729
comments.body: I think for normal quality it's sufficient if you *work* with Ai instead of just try to one shot assets. Artists are incredibly expensive and understand you less than AI and you'll need very, very experienced and expensive artists if you want quality work

comments.author: WolfedUpLlama
comments.body:
Adding the general public is more forgiving and or blissful to AI-coded projects compared to AI visuals. (I’m a motion designer in advertising for context)

Same thing from what I’ve seen in the book community. Readers tend to despise books written by AI.

Guess the way I look at it is if there 100 people willing to buy a game and 40 do not want AI visuals, you’ve cut your chances to 60 people compared to none AI visuals, i can’t imagine there are pro AI people who aren’t going to play a game that doesn’t us actually visuals made from a human.

comments.author: Kiran__reddit
comments.body: if you love art absolutely, Games are one of human's best creation.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
yes but it is "art direction", "art taste" (basically design) and not "how to use this custom brush to do easy shading" or "this one layer trick will simplify your workflow" etc

I have been reviewing AI games and I can tell you that people with a design background stand out pretty well. 

On the other hand, devs with a tech background (you can guess which group I belong to) tend to make similar mistakes: has poor color choices like they are color blind, mishandling pixel art because "close enough" etc

so AI devs with art/design background are eating well rn

I am not sure how one grinds "design" but that is what you need to stand out

comments.author: Apalala__
comments.body:
the stronger you are at defining art terms and techniques,  
the better you reason out to AI how to create specific things.

comments.author: Xanma_6aki
comments.body: Making asset does not take that long also while ai can make decent assets in 3d people hate it much more than they hate ai code for some reason

comments.author: EchoingAngel
comments.body: AI can do art, but there's quite a few limitations that you need to be aware of before you get too deep into how visuals/animations work in your game. Animations are rough, smooth surfaces are rough, and making coherent "families" are really hard currently. These things massively affected my design decisions. So don't spend too much time on a barebones game until you have an idea of what AI can get you

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
AI art, at best, is serviceable right now. I've been happy with a few pieces, but I know for a fact that if I could afford it, those same pieces would have been much better done by an artist.

If you can afford an artist, hire an artist. Period. The work will look better, and there are a huge number of benefits from that kind of collab that you will never get from the machine (example: the artist will also want to promote your game since their work is featured in it, so now you have multiple people in different social circles expanding the game's presence).

Also, 99% of the time - even with decent AI generations - the art still looks like AI art, because the machine has its own stylistic tendencies, and that's a major turn-off for most people (right now).

comments.author: Able_Zombie_7859
comments.body: Human made content will arguably become MORE valuable in the face of a torrent of ai content

comments.author: OakNLeaf
comments.body:
That's why you don't make the assets on your own. The problem with just letting AI do it is that you end up with AI slop. 

AI Slop makes it look like you don't care about your product regardless of how much time you have spent polishing your games features. 

My process is going to be to use AI for placeholders (I haven't started the prototype process yet) using a Style Guide I created and then when I get a art style I like I will pay Artist to help create the Art. 

Obviously that's my own process, I don't expect anyone else to do it, but I want to have as little AI facing the actual user I can, so anything UI/text based that is visible to the user I want an actual human to make.

comments.author: GameNotFound
comments.body: In this current climate, you mention AI and people will riot (and not necessarily for bad reason). This should also be considered when contemplating integrating AI into your work flow.
